h: Takabuti, dinosaurs and the Botanic Gardens
p: One of the museum's most famous residents is Takabuti, an Egyptian mummy who arrived in Belfast in the 1830s and has fascinated visitors ever since. Scientific research in recent years has revealed new details about her life and death, and she remains a real crowd-pleaser. Dinosaur fans should look out for the skeleton of the Edmontosaurus, which towers over younger visitors.

Allow two to three hours for a decent look round, though families can easily spend longer. With the galleries spread over several floors, it's smart to pick a few favourites rather than trying to see everything in one go. There's a café when you need a break, and the museum is set up well for pushchairs and wheelchairs.

Step outside and you're straight into the Botanic Gardens, one of the city's best-loved green spaces. Don't miss the Palm House, a beautiful curved Victorian glasshouse, and the Tropical Ravine, where you look down into a sunken jungle of exotic plants. Both make a lovely add-on, and the lawns are perfect for a picnic on a sunny day.

Just beyond the gardens is Queen's University, with the striking red-brick Lanyon Building at its heart. The surrounding Queen's Quarter is buzzing with cafés, bars and restaurants, especially along Botanic Avenue, so you're never short of somewhere to eat afterwards. The city centre is an easy walk or short bus ride away.
